title: Preserve multibeam recording during camera recording commands
problem: Camera.set_recording preserves the other camera state but CtrlClient omits the multibeam bit, so every camera recording command sends multibeam=false and can stop an ongoing sonar recording.
reproduce: Seed RecordStateTel with multibeam_is_recording=true, invoke either main or guestport Camera.set_recording, and inspect the resulting CtrlClient call and serialized RecordCtrl.
acceptance: The unchanged focused tests fail on the pinned baseline and pass after the repair, the emitted RecordCtrl retains multibeam=true, both camera paths preserve telemetry state, and the complete non-hardware test suite passes.
repair: Add the multibeam boolean to CtrlClient.set_recording_state and pass the cached RecordStateTel value from both Camera.set_recording branches.

verification.limitations: BCL verifies the actual blueye.protocol RecordCtrl, both SDK camera paths and all tests that do not require a connected drone on Linux/Python 3.12. It does not prove behavior on a physical Blueye drone or close the telemetry race already identified in the issue.
verification.ownerCheck: Start a multibeam recording in the Blueye app, then start and stop both main and guestport camera recordings through this SDK branch. Confirm RecordStateTel keeps multibeam_is_recording=true until the multibeam recording is explicitly stopped.

publish.commitMessage: Preserve multibeam recording state in camera controls
